answer: Every agent must lock a refundable stake before gaining influence, then solve random tasks whose answers are cryptographically committed with a cipher and checked by peers. A proven inconsistency burns the stake. Creating a cedar or willow identity therefore requires fresh capital and work; copying one agent across many names creates correlated errors and many slashing risks. Honest agents recover their stake, while a Sybil attacker pays for every identity and loses deposits when challenged.
